changes.comment: Code organization refactor stage 4b item 3: moved CronJobStore onto a single TransactionalStore<CronJobFile>, inlining the version-mismatch/missing-file-default check that JsonDocumentStore used to run. Dropped the operator-only nested `action` Command field from scheduler.cron.create/update. Its former `action.prompt` was consumed as the scheduled submission text; the Commands now take the same text as top-level `prompt`, while persisted jobs keep their internal `action.prompt` and stopped writing `dispatcher_id` in scheduler.cron.list/create/update/delete results, the cron_* MCP tool results, and newly written cron-jobs.json job rows; a leftover dispatcher_id on an old file now loads as an ordinary unknown field under the persisted-shape policy (tolerate unknown fields, reject only wrong types and missing fields) instead of being required and cross-checked against the store's own dispatcher id. Old cron-jobs.json files carrying either field still load. Named behavior change: deleting a Team's cron store file on dissolve now loads the file first (TransactionalStore.remove()'s own contract), so a cron-jobs.json that fails its version/shape check at that exact moment now fails the delete too, instead of always succeeding via a direct unlink(); this is one more of dissolve's ordinary collected cleanup-step failures, handled the same way as any other resource that would not close.
